summary: Front light of a 1907 range pair at the mouth of the Cocagne River, New Brunswick; discontinued in 2018 and moved to the Cocagne Marina in 2019.

light.characteristic: fixed red (1907 front light, 6th order French lens, per the 1908 list of lights)

structures.note: Rowlett: 7.5 m (25 ft) tower; the 1907 Department description gives 28 ft (8.5 m) from base to vane.
First a light on a pole (1907 description); a modern skeletal rear tower about 13 m (43 ft) later (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).

access.note: Front light at the Cocagne Marina; grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner, per LighthouseFriends); Cocagne Marina (owner and site manager of the rear light, per Rowlett)

events.note: Department lists range lights at Cocagne among works under way, to be established.
Range lights completed by day labour at a cost of $699.17 (LighthouseFriends dates completion to 1907; the Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1908 records it).
Front light listed as a 240 degree, 6th order French lens with a duplex lamp, red.
Front tower showed a fixed yellow light; the modern skeletal rear light with a white daymark and red stripe served as the rear range light.
Range lights discontinued in 2018 (LighthouseFriends); front light inactive since 2018 (Rowlett).
Front light moved from the south end of the NB 134 bridge to the Cocagne Marina across the river entrance, 26 July 2019 (LighthouseFriends); restored there (Rowlett).

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the range lights were discontinued in 2018; Rowlett says the front light has been inactive since 2018. The current Coast Guard list for this stretch (Northumberland Strait West, as read 2026-10-28) carries buoys and the Cap-de-Cocagne wharf light but no Cocagne range entry.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and Rowlett agree the range was discontinued in 2018. LighthouseFriends dates the move to the marina to 26 July 2019; Rowlett says it was relocated after the 2018 deactivation, with no date. Both are kept.

LighthouseFriends dates completion to 1907. The Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1907 says the range lights 'will be established', and the report for the year ended 30 June 1908 says they were completed, so the work falls between July 1907 and June 1908.

notes_for_editor: Keeper link (Dominique Goguen, printed 'D. Gognen') is matched by position in an OCR table where names, dates and salaries are in separate blocks; the 1909, 1910, 1911 and 1915 keeper lists show the same name at the same place, so the reading is consistent but a human should look at the scan page 73 of the FY1915 report. The Department's lists in the local corpus end in 1924, so keepers after 1926 come from LighthouseFriends only. The 1907 description gives visibility in miles as printed (not converted). Coordinates: the record's point (OSM node 1659450444, 46.335587 -64.614206) is about 0.9 km from the LighthouseFriends coordinates, which mark the current marina site; the record point is probably the historic site at the bridge, so no correction proposed. The Coast Guard's Northumberland Strait West list (cached copy, read 2026-10-28) does not carry the Cocagne range entries (record CCG number A1116, admiralty H1354), which is consistent with discontinuance, but the list edition date was not visible. Rowlett's front-tower height (7.5 m) differs from the 1907 base-to-vane figure (28 ft); both are kept. No wrecks or storms tied to the range were found in the Department reports in the local corpus (1900-1924); newspapers were not searched (Chronicling America holds US papers). The living-person rule applies to the later keepers, named in public role only. Verified 2026-10-28 by the fact-checker: the FY1915 keepers' list page image (scan 73) was read. In the NB agency table the station and keeper columns run in the same row order, and counting from the first station the 23rd row is 'Cocagne range' with 'D. Gognen, Oct. 14, 1907, 220 00', so the position match holds. The FY1906 heading reads 'w under way' in the OCR (the story says 'works under way'). Current Coast Guard list checked: List of Lights, Buoys and Fog Signals, Atlantic Coast, Northumberland Strait West, 2026 edition, monthly edition 09/2026 (https://www.notmar.gc.ca/publications/list-lights/atl/atl1085e.pdf): it carries Cocagne Harbour and Cocagne River buoys and the Cap-de-Cocagne wharf light (1114) and no Cocagne range entry, which supports the discontinuance correction. The story now states that the 2012 rear light also showed a yellow light, as LighthouseFriends says.
